new_class_descriptions.Similarity-based: Reduces/orders a test suite by measuring the similarity (or diversity) between test cases themselves, e.g. a distance over test source code text or command-line input, and keeping an evenly spread/maximally dissimilar subset (clustering, k-means++, coresets, adaptive random testing, minhash). It does not need code coverage, models or requirements, so it is black-box and scalable; evaluated with fault detection loss, reduction ratio and execution time. Limitation: effectiveness depends on how well textual/structural distance reflects fault-revealing behaviour.

evaluation metric: APFD, relative ratio to optimal, paired t-test, Cohen's d, runtime
notes: Hybrid: behavioural (digraph/MBT) model plus probabilistic HMM; also proposes accumulated Q-value ordering. Parameters (gamma=0.9, eps=0.8, R RHMM package, hardware) described, no replication package URL. 1000 repetitions per technique. Faults for first 4 apps taken from AutoBlackTest study.
title: Test Case Prioritization Using Extended Digraphs
author: Emam, Seyedeh Sepideh and Miller, James

evaluation metric: APFD, testing time, number of potential/real races detected, percentage of tests selected

author: Yu, Tingting and Srisa-an, Witawas and Rothermel, Gregg

new_class_descriptions.Information Retrieval-based: Selects or orders tests by recovering trace links between test artefacts (e.g. natural-language manual test descriptions, test code) and code artefacts using textual similarity techniques (TF-IDF, latent semantic indexing, topic models), often combined with change information. Tests linked to changed or untested code are chosen or ranked high, without needing execution coverage data. Typically evaluated by link accuracy/precision or fault detection; limited by vocabulary mismatch and identifier quality.

algorithm_family: information retrieval / NLP (latent semantic indexing: term-document matrix + SVD, Porter stemming + stop-word removal, similarity table) + program analysis (static call graph propagation)
objectives: single-objective (cover changed-but-untested methods with suggested tests)
sut: Business information system at Munich Re (industrial, C#, web application): 340 KLOC, 39,398 methods, 10 years old; 4 manual natural-language test cases (5-11 steps, executing 1,297-2,300 methods each, 2,711 methods in total)
leveraged feature: natural-language test case text, method signatures (camelCase concepts), static call graph (IL code), method-level code changes (IL diff), change coverage from profiling data
notes: Not covered by Yoo and Harman classes (closest: Modification-based / Requirement-Based, but core is IR trace-link recovery). Initial evaluation only (1 system, 4 tests); evaluates trace link quality, not fault detection. Details (Porter stemming, gap cut-off) given, no code link.
title: Selecting manual regression test cases automatically using trace link recovery and change coverage
author: Eder, Sebastian and Hauptmann, Benedikt and Junker, Maximilian and Vaas, Rudolf and Prommer, Karl-Heinz

sut: JMock (open source Java): ~5 KLOC, 504 JUnit test cases, 92% coverage, 6 manually seeded refactoring-fault versions (Add Parameter, Extract Method, Move Method, Pull Up Field, Pull Up Method, Rename Method)
leveraged feature: type and location of refactoring edit, refactoring fault models (affected methods), per-test call graphs (methods covered), two program versions

author: Alves, Everton L. G. and Machado, Patricia D. L. and Massoni, Tiago and Santos, Samuel T. C.

author: Butool, Rimsha and Nadeem, Aamer and Sindhu, Muddassar and Zaman, Oamar uz

author: Vats, Prashant and Gossain, Anjana and Mandot, Manju

evaluation metric: execution time, reduction rate, fitness value

sut: 12 industrial CI datasets (from Yang et al.): Apache Commons (457 tests, 423 cycles), Drill (556, 376), Parquet (273, 1190), Tajo (314, 4125), DSpace (106, 3230), Google Auto (46, 530), Google Closure (360, 2257), Google Guava (433, 772), IOF/ROL (1941, 320), Mybatis (303, 899), Paintcontrol (89, 352), Rails (2010, 3263); failure rates 0.02%-28.79%
leveraged feature: test execution history (verdicts, duration, last execution), whether a test case is new, reward on first executions of new tests
notes: Extension of RETECS (Spieker et al.); parameters follow Spieker (time limit, depth, training steps), 30 repetitions; no code/data link in text -> 0.5. Selection under budget inherent to RETECS but paper frames it as prioritization.
title: Focus on New Test Cases in Continuous Integration Testing based on Reinforcement Learning
author: Chen, Fanliang and Li, Zheng and Shang, Ying and Yang, Yang

algorithm_family: heuristic (greedy graph traversal over a Jaccard-weighted test graph)
objectives: single-objective (aggregated: node value = coverage/time plus Jaccard-distance edge value; authors call it two-goal: fault detection rate and execution time)
sut: nopCommerce (open source, ASP.NET): 226,354 LOC, 543 tests, 40 real faults, 4 versions; Umbraco-CMS (open source, C#): 128,037 LOC, 3,381 tests, 30 real faults, 4 versions; jmeter (SIR): 43,400 LOC, 78 tests, 9 seeded faults, 7 versions; jtopas (SIR): 5,400 LOC, 128 tests, 5 seeded faults, 5 versions
leveraged feature: statement coverage, test execution time, test dissimilarity (Jaccard distance on coverage)
evaluation metric: APFD, execution time to reveal 100% of faults, percentage of test suite run to reveal 100% of faults
notes: No replication package (URLs only for subjects). Compared with total/additional statement and Jaccard dissimilarity prioritization under 25/50/75% time budgets. Dissimilarity part is not cleanly covered by a class; kept Coverage-Based + Cost-Aware.
title: Graphite: A Greedy Graph-Based Technique for Regression Test Case Prioritization
author: Azizi, Maral and Do, Hyunsook

algorithm_family: meta-heuristic (NSGA-II, jMetal) + information retrieval / NLP (Latent Semantic Indexing with SVD, cosine similarity, k=300, for traceability recovery) + metric-based maintainability index (software quality model)
objectives: multi-objective (maximize weighted code coverage AUC, maximize weighted requirements coverage AUC, minimize cumulative execution cost AUC)
sut: 21 Java open-source applications (Apache projects, iTrust, JTidy, Jabref, etc.): 2 KLOC to 138 KLOC, 33 to 2,307 JUnit tests, 10 to 31 requirements, 10 to 22 injected faults per app (derived from bug trackers); e.g. LaTazza 2k/33/12 faults, iTrust 15k/919/21, Xerces 138k/376/20
leveraged feature: statement coverage, requirements coverage (via LSI traceability links), test execution time, code and requirements metrics (CBO, RFC, LCOM, WMC, scattering, tangling...) giving a maintainability index as fault-proneness weights
evaluation metric: APFD, APFD on severe faults (ftype1), APFD on faults of relevant requirements (ftype2)
notes: Parameters given (pop=2*suite size, 1000 iterations, crossover 0.9) but no replication package link (only tool names MOTCP+/SWTMetrics, project sites of subjects). Core principle = requirements+code coverage with cost; no exact class.
title: A Multi-Objective Technique to Prioritize Test Cases
author: Marchetto, Alessandro and Islam, Md. Mahfuzul and Asghar, Waseem and Susi, Angelo and Scanniello, Giuseppe

algorithm_family: heuristic (greedy/rule-based weighted score sorting)
objectives: single-objective (aggregated weight per test: failure frequency, failure impact, cross-functional coverage, execution time; paper writes it as a 4-component objective g)
sut: 3 industrial Android mobile device systems (A1, A2, A3): 2,985 / 3,250 / 3,327 LOC, 501 / 653 / 700 manually specified tests, 5 consecutive CI executions of history; compared with manual ordering by 5 test experts
leveraged feature: test failure history (frequency and recency), failure impact/severity, test execution time budget, cross-functional (feature interaction) coverage
evaluation metric: APFDc, number of failures detected in time slices, cumulative failure impact, failure frequency, cross-functional coverage
notes: Only formulas, no parameter values, language or tooling; no replication package. Black-box, no source code. Weights tunable. Alternatively could be seen as multi-objective (4 criteria) but a single ranking weight is computed.
title: Multi-perspective Regression Test Prioritization for Time-Constrained Environments
author: Marijan, Dusica

algorithm_family: heuristic (greedy: total, additional and iterative strategies)
objectives: single-objective (maximize fault detection rate)
sut: 8 WS-BPEL applications (benchmark from prior work): atm, buybook, dslservice, gymlocker, loanapproval, marketplace, purchase, triphandling; 23-153 elements, 52-532 LOC each, 60 modified versions (43 used) with one seeded fault each (value/decision/statement mutation); 1000 random tests per pool, 100 test suites per subject (mean size 86.8)
leveraged feature: coverage of BPEL activities, BPEL workflow transitions, XPath selections, XRG (XPath Rewriting Graph) nodes, WSDL elements
notes: Mainly an empirical study of factors (strategy, artifact type, order direction, executable vs non-executable) in average vs adverse scenarios; also introduces 4 new XRG-based techniques (M5-M8), so classified as Coverage-Based. title: Is XML-Based Test Case Prioritization for Validating WS-BPEL Evolution Effective in Both Average and Adverse Scenarios?
author: Jia, Changjiang and Mei, Lijun and Chan, W.K. and Yu, Y.T. and Tse, T.H.

algorithm_family: heuristic (greedy reduction + test merging and redundant INSERT removal, rule-based)
objectives: single-objective (minimize number of tests/INSERTs subject to preserving coverage of test requirements)
sut: 34 relational database schemas (open-source, government, website examples; e.g. iTrust, BookTown, JWhoisServer, WordNet, StackOverflow): 1-42 tables, 3-309 columns, 1-134 integrity constraints; test suites generated with SchemaAnalyst (AVM-D and DOMINO), e.g. iTrust 1,517 tests, BookTown 269 tests; 30 repetitions
leveraged feature: test requirements coverage (ClauseAICC+ANCC+AUCC integrity-constraint coverage), database setup/INSERT statement overlap between tests
evaluation metric: reduction rate (tests and INSERT statements), mutation score, execution time (suite and mutation analysis)

Coverage-Based chosen as principle is coverage preservation; merging of similar tests is an extra step (could suit Similarity-based but it is not distance-based).

author: Alsharif, Abdullah and Kapfhammer, Gregory M. and McMinn, Phil

algorithm_family: machine learning (linear regression, normal equation, 2 features) + information retrieval / NLP (TF-IDF similarity between test coverage elements and changed elements)

leveraged feature: line/branch/method coverage, coverage frequency (TF), test uniqueness of covered elements (IDF), changed files between versions, past fault data for regression training
notes: IRCOV model. Registry class 'Information Retrieval-based' was proposed for selection via trace links; reused here with imperfect fit (TF-IDF on coverage elements as documents/queries). No replication package; parameters described.

author: Kwon, Jung-Hyun and Ko, In-Young and Rothermel, Gregg and Staats, Matt

objectives: multi-objective (maximize method coverage, minimize coverage overlap, maximize historical performance-change size); single-objective GA variant aggregates the 3 by equal-weight sum
sut: 10 open-source Java JMH microbenchmark suites (dataset of Laaber et al.): Byte Buddy, Eclipse Collections, JCTools, Jenetics, Log4j 2, Netty, Okio, RxJava, Xodus, Zipkin; 161 versions, 1,829 distinct microbenchmarks / 6,460 distinct parameterizations (59,164 total); ~31 to ~2,371 benchmarks per version; suite runtimes 0.26 to 38.45 h; faults = measured performance changes between adjacent versions

evaluation metric: APFD-P, prioritization time overhead, analysis time overhead
notes: Replication package [58] + bencher v0.4.0 stated in text (URL not in extracted list; refs removed). Empirical evaluation of new SBSMBP/Greedy techniques for performance microbenchmarks; objectives mix coverage and history.
title: Evaluating Search-Based Software Microbenchmark Prioritization
author: Laaber, Christoph and Yue, Tao and Ali, Shaukat

leveraged feature: statement-level coverage of previous version, code churn (diff between versions)

author: Altiero, Francesco and Colella, Giovanni and Corazza, Anna and Di Martino, Sergio and Peron, Adriano and Starace, Luigi L. L.

author: Wang, Dingbang and Zhao, Yu and Xiao, Lu and Yu, Tingting

notes: Extends RETECS (reward redesign). ANN agent, 30 repetitions, time budget 50%; no replication package. Pure prioritization with time-limit adjustment.

author: Shi, Tingting and Xiao, Lei and Wu, Keshou

algorithm_family: fuzzy logic (Mamdani fuzzy inference system, centre-of-area defuzzification, jFuzzyLogic) + meta-heuristic (Ant Colony Optimization, MAX-MIN Ant System solving TSP formulation)

leveraged feature: cyclomatic complexity and instability (coupling) of components, function-level coverage (gcov), fault detection history, test execution time

author: Silva, Dennis Sávio and Rabelo, Ricardo and Neto, Pedro Santos and Britto, Ricardo and Oliveira, Pedro Almir

leveraged feature: test failure history (FailRate, LastVerdict, LastFailAge, TransitionRate), execution time/duration, test age, assertion/exception rates, lines inserted/deleted, commit count

author: Khan, Md Asif and Azim, Akramul and Liscano, Ramiro and Smith, Kevin and Chang, Yee-Kang and Seferi, Gkerta and Tauseef, Qasim

leveraged feature: number of faults detected per test, test execution time (fault rate), fault severity weight
evaluation metric: APFD, percentage of test cases needed to detect all faults

leveraged feature: number of modified lines executed by each test (diff-based), test execution time, number of inheritance edges covered; time budget (50 min)
notes: Time-aware knapsack formulation (modified lines per unit time) so Cost-Aware; also change-based. GA params given (pop 200, pc 0.35, pm 0.10, 75 gens, NSGA-II); no code link. Table 1 with sizes missing from extracted text.

sut: 8 WS-BPEL service applications (IBM BPEL repository, BPWS4J, Oracle, WS Innovation Framework): atm, gymlocker, loanapproval, marketplace, purchase, triphandling, buybook, dslservice; 43 modified versions with seeded faults (BPEL/XPath/WSDL mutations); 1,000-test pool per benchmark, 100 test suites each; evolution points at 40/60/80% of suite

author: Mei, Lijun and Chan, W.K. and Tse, T.H. and Jiang, Bo and Zhai, Ke

objectives: single-objective (fault detection rate; cascaded sort: change frequency, then fault history, then execution rate)
sut: 2 component-based projects, >14,000 LOC total: online shopping management system (synthetic data) and healthcare device application (real data from a local software house, industrial); thousands of tests per suite; 16 and 40 participants; sizes per project not reported

evaluation metric: APFD, fault detection rate, questionnaire satisfaction

title: Model-based test case prioritization using cluster analysis: a soft-computing approach

algorithm_family: clustering (agglomerative hierarchical, average linkage, Euclidean distance on binary coverage vectors, predefined number of clusters) + heuristic (greedy/rule-based)
objectives: single-objective (aggregated: weighted sum of code coverage, code complexity and requirement complexity; clusters ordered by change relevance)
sut: Launch Interceptor Program (LIP, anti-missile system, academic/Syracuse): 40 methods, 14 decision nodes, 48 test cases; 4 simulated code changes (segments S4, S14, S20, S31)
leveraged feature: segment traversal vectors of test cases (coverage), code change location, flow-graph reachability from changed segment, code complexity, user requirement complexity
notes: Clusters tests by coverage-profile distance (Distribution-Based) then ranks clusters by change relevance and tests by coverage/complexity. C# code listed in paper appendix (partial, DB-dependent), no repository link, so 0.5. Authors also say 'reduced subset' but method orders all tests.
title: Regression Test Cases Prioritization Using Clustering and Code Change Relevance

new_class_descriptions.Risk-based: Selects or prioritizes test cases (or test paths) according to the risk exposure of the parts of the system they exercise, typically risk probability times damage cost attached to model elements (states, requirements, components), often combined with change information. Tests covering high-risk and changed elements are executed first, low-risk/unchanged ones are discarded or postponed. Usually illustrated on small case studies; limited by subjective risk estimation.

algorithm_family: fuzzy logic (rule-based fuzzy expert system: triangular membership functions, min/max AND/OR operators, 4 risk x 2 change linguistic rules; inference type not named)
objectives: single-objective (aggregated: fuzzy combination of risk exposure and change value into one test-path category)
sut: ATM UML state machine diagram, illustrative example before/after Aadhaar fingerprint enhancement (academic example): 3 test paths; no LOC/faults
leveraged feature: UML state machine converted to weighted EFSM, risk exposure (probability x damage cost) per state, change in model (weights on changed nodes)
notes: Output retestable > reusable, obsolete discarded: selection plus ordering, UML-design based (Design-based also plausible). Risk exposure is the distinguishing principle, hence new class Risk-based. No empirical evaluation.
title: Fuzzy Expert System Based Test Cases Prioritization from UML State Machine Diagram using Risk Information

algorithm_family: heuristic (greedy/rule-based) (global max-min distance, ART-like, O(n^2))
objectives: single-objective (maximize diversity: test with largest minimal distance to already prioritized set)
sut: 4 C programs (SIR): print_tokens 341-343 LOC, 4130 tests, 7 faulty versions; print_tokens2 350-355 LOC, 4115 tests, 10 versions; make 12609-17153 LOC, 1043 tests, 33 versions; sed 4711-9204 LOC, 370 tests, 18 versions (Fig. labels mention schedule/schedule2 inconsistently)
leveraged feature: branch coverage vectors (gcov) of test cases, pairwise distance (Euclidean, cosine, Jaccard, Gower-Legendre, Sokal-Sneath, proportional distance)
evaluation metric: NAPFD, APFD, standard deviation of NAPFD, ANOVA/multiple comparison
notes: Registry class Similarity-based reused although registered for minimization (it also covers ordering by diversity); inputs are coverage vectors, so Coverage-Based is a partial alternative. No replication link; gcov, 100 repetitions, sampling 2-20%.
title: Similarity-based regression test case prioritization

algorithm_family: program analysis (deterministic static/dynamic analysis) (ESDG forward slicing)
objectives: single-objective (select modification-revealing tests, i.e. maximize inclusiveness/precision)
sut: 3 Java programs x 3 versions = 9 subjects: Cruise Control (SIR): 283-339 LOC, 10-15 tests, 36-167 mutants; Binary Search Tree (sanfoundry blog): 293-343 LOC, 17-22 tests, 52-119 mutants; ATM (Java How to Program book): 670-770 LOC, 23-28 tests, 49-191 mutants
leveraged feature: extended system dependence graph (ESDG), changed statements (muJava mutants), affected statements via forward slicing, test coverage information
evaluation metric: precision, inclusiveness, FEP, percentage of selected tests
notes: Graph-walk chosen (traverses ESDG for OO programs); SDG slicing/Dynamic-slicing are alternatives. Changes simulated by mutants. muJava/JDK1.7/hardware stated, no replication package.
title: Regression Test Cases selection for Object-Oriented Programs based on Affected Statements

algorithm_family: meta-heuristic (search-based: evolutionary) (NSGA-II) + information retrieval / NLP (LSI traceability recovery)
objectives: multi-objective (maximize code coverage, maximize requirements coverage, minimize execution cost)
sut: 3 Java applications (distributed online, used in literature): AveCalc 8 classes, 1827 LOC, 10 requirements, 47 JUnit tests, 15 injected faults; LaTazza 18 classes, 1121 LOC, 10 reqs, 33 tests, 15 faults; iTrust 232 classes, 15495 LOC, 15 reqs, 919 tests, 21 faults
leveraged feature: code coverage, requirements coverage (weighted, with requirement dependencies), test execution time, LSI-based traceability links among requirements, code and tests
evaluation metric: reduced suite size, number of revealed faults, rFDC, sensitivity (faults on relevant requirements), efficiency (faults/time), code coverage, requirements coverage, diversity (Levenshtein), robustness
notes: Hybrid of requirement coverage and cost-aware Pareto optimisation; code coverage is also an objective (limit of two classes). Parameters given (pop=2x suite size, k=300, crossover 0.9), no replication package.
title: A Multi-Objective Technique for Test Suite Reduction

algorithm_family: clustering (agglomerative hierarchical clustering, Euclidean distance on statement-coverage vectors, average linkage) + heuristic (greedy/rule-based scheduling with dynamic fault-detection-rate adjustment and timeout mechanism)
objectives: single-objective (maximize fault detection rate / APFD)
sut: 12 C programs (SIR): 7 Siemens programs (print_tokens, print_tokens2, replace, schedule, schedule2, tcas, totinfo; >=1,000 tests each, print_tokens ~4,000), space (2,000 sampled tests), and flex, sed, grep, gzip; versions with 0-31 hand-seeded faults. Per-program LOC in an image table (not in text)
leveraged feature: statement coverage of test cases, historical fault detection rates from previous versions, textual diff of changed lines (to estimate current fault detection), waiting time of candidate tests
notes: Clustering by coverage + history-based fault rates, so hybrid of Coverage-Based and History-Based. Parameters (clusters ~1% of tests, wt_max) and environment given; no replication package (only sir.unl.edu).
title: Coverage-Based Clustering and Scheduling Approach for Test Case Prioritization

algorithm_family: machine learning (supervised ANN classifier, 2 hidden layers of 20 units, Keras)
objectives: single-objective (predict priority class of each test to maximize early fault detection)
sut: Credit Card Approval System (from literature, Java/JUnit): 48 requirements, 416 tests, 3 versions with 3/4/5 seeded faults; Registration-Verifier application (from literature, Java/JUnit): 70 requirements, 523 tests, 2 versions with 7/9 seeded faults
leveraged feature: number of modified modules covered by test, modified-module sequence, test case complexity (number of covered branch requirements), number of modified requirements (changed conditions) and sequence, test inputs and expected results
evaluation metric: APFD, accuracy, precision, recall, test suite reduction rate, training/classification time, percentage of tests needed to detect faults
notes: Version-specific; selects tests with MM>=1 then ANN ranks into 3 priority classes whose labels derive from MM+MR (supervised). Taxonomy fit imperfect: ML on change and complexity features. Python 3.4/Keras, no link.
title: Version specific test case prioritization approach based on artificial neural network

algorithm_family: meta-heuristic (search-based: Genetic Algorithm with elitist + roulette-wheel selection, one-point crossover, random mutation; implemented in MATLAB)
objectives: single-objective (aggregated fitness = primary code coverage x100 + secondary coverage-over-time measure)
sut: Not described: a Java program with JUnit tests (execution time via Ant/JUnit, coverage via EclEmma); test-case table (time, coverage) given only as image; compared with random, goal-oriented and path-oriented prioritization. No LOC/tests/faults reported
leveraged feature: test execution time, code coverage (incremental), customer-designated severe test cases
notes: Time-aware GA; customer-severe tests are fixed into the suite and GA selects/orders the rest (selection+ordering under time budget; classified prioritization as per title). Weak empirical section, no APFD. GA operator probabilities listed but values not shown.
title: Analysis of Test Case Prioritization in Regression Testing using Genetic Algorithm

algorithm_family: meta-heuristic (search-based: Clonal Selection Algorithm, artificial immune system)
objectives: single-objective (maximize APFDc as affinity: fault severity, test cost, fault detection aggregated)
sut: Hospital management application (industrial, Versionsquare Pvt Ltd, Java), 5 sequential versions: 11,450/10,278/9,876/8,770/6,550 LOC, 8/7/5/7/4 hand-seeded faults, one suite of 300 tests
leveraged feature: test execution cost (time), faults detected by past runs, fault severity (historical information)
notes: Parameters given (pop 200, 500 generations, mutation operators), Java app, no replication package or URLs. Hybrid cost-cognizant + history-based; metaheuristic is CSA.
title: Cost Cognizant History Based Prioritization of Test Case for Regression Testing

algorithm_family: meta-heuristic (search-based: Ant Colony Optimization with modified probability formula)
objectives: single-objective (aggregated: maximize fault coverage, minimize execution time in one transition probability)
sut: Illustrative example only: 8 test cases, 10 faults, execution times 2-7 min (toy data, not a real SUT)
leveraged feature: faults covered by each test case, test execution time
notes: Titled selection+prioritization but no code changes used: picks min-time set covering all faults (set cover) = minimization, then orders. Parameter names listed without values; no code/language. Fault coverage treated as coverage criterion.
title: Ants Optimization for Minimal Test Case Selection and Prioritization as to Reduce the Cost of Regression Testing

algorithm_family: reinforcement learning (Deep Q-Network: Q-learning with a deep neural network, experience replay and target network; DeepRP; compared with DeepGini, Hansie, DeepOrder, LogTCP, RL-TCP)
objectives: single-objective (maximize cumulative reward, i.e. rank-distance to optimal ordering)
sut: Paint Control (industrial, ABB Robotics): 114 tests, 312 CI cycles, 25,594 verdicts, 19.36% failed; IOF/ROL (industrial): 2,086 tests, 320 CI cycles, 30,319 verdicts, 28.43% failed; GSDTSR (Google Shared Dataset of Test Suite Results): 5,555 tests, 336 cycles, 1,260,617 verdicts, 0.25% failed
leveraged feature: test execution history (pass/fail verdicts), source code changes, version control info, code coverage, test steps/commands weighted coverage graph
evaluation metric: APFD, APFDc, APFD_TA, RMSE, execution time
notes: CI history-based TCP with DRL. Python 3.7.8, hyperparameters in Table 5 (episodes 700, lr 0.001, batch 64) but no code link -> 0.5. Reported RMSE of NAPFD vs ideal.
title: An Improved Deep Learning Based Test Case Prioritization Using Deep Reinforcement Learning

algorithm_family: hybrid (meta-heuristic: Bee Colony Optimization + Genetic Algorithm crossover)
objectives: single-objective (minimize execution time subject to covering all faults)
sut: Illustrative example only: 8 test cases, 10 faults, execution times 2-7 min (toy data); claims several examples tested but only one shown
leveraged feature: faults covered by each test case (binary vector), test execution time
evaluation metric: execution time, number of faults covered
notes: Called test case selection/reduction but finds min-time subset covering all faults (set cover), not change-based, so minimization. No parameters, tool or URLs; no real evaluation.
title: Regression Test Suite Reduction using an Hybrid Technique Based on BCO And Genetic Algorithm

algorithm_family: fuzzy logic (fuzzy sets AFFECTED and EFFECTIVENESS with S-function membership, alpha=0, beta=0.4*N_A, gamma=0.8*N_A; Assertion Violating Potential = 1 - membership)
objectives: single-objective (maximize Assertion Violating Potential / rate of assertion violation)
sut: 9 Java programs with assertions (from Korel et al.): Concatenation (19 LOC, 4 assertions, 4 versions); Average (54 LOC, 7, 3); RestrictedAverage (50, 6, 4); FunnyAverage (30, 5, 3); RealNumberFormat (39, 5, 5); Bank (336 LOC, 15, 9); MinMax (23, 3, 6); Total (52, 8, 3); RestrictedSubstitute (29, 3, 3); 40 modified versions in total, 150 test suites generated by assertion-oriented test generation, seeded faults
leveraged feature: assertion revalidation analysis (slicing-based: Affected / Partially Affected / Not Affected assertions by number of modified variables), history of test cases from original-version assertion-oriented testing
evaluation metric: WAPVA (weighted average percentage of violated assertions)
notes: Assertion-/property-oriented prioritization, closest to 'Others' (property-based: tests likely to violate assertions). Test suites also 'subset selection' mentioned but method reorders. Params for S-function given, no replication package. | merged: second extraction proposed Assertion-based; kept Others (property-based).
title: Using Fuzzy Logic in Test Case Prioritization for Regression Testing Programs with Assertions

algorithm_family: reinforcement learning (LSTM-based agent, experience replay, gradient projection/SVD reconciliation, Mann-Whitney change detection)
objectives: single-objective (maximize NAPFD via APHF reward plus additional reward)
sut: 12 industrial CI datasets (RETECS-style, from prior CI-TCP studies): Apache Commons (457 tests, 423 cycles), Drill (556, 376), Parquet (273, 1190), Tajo (314, 4125), Dspace (106, 3230), Google Auto (46, 530), Closure (360, 2257), Guava (433, 772), IOF/ROL (1941, 320), Mybatis (303, 899), Paint Control (89, 352), Rails (2010, 3263); failure rates 0.02-28.79%
leveraged feature: test case metadata and execution results of the last 7 CI cycles (history), failure history, NAPFD fluctuation between cycles
notes: Replication package: https://github.com/1394827282/EAA/. CI time budget (50% of duration) so implicit selection, but classified as prioritization. History-Based fit reasonable (execution history), principle is RL adaptation.
title: An Environment Adaptation Agent of Reinforcement Learning in Continuous Integration Test Case Prioritization

algorithm_family: heuristic (greedy/rule-based: weighted sum of six requirement factors, then sort)
objectives: single-objective (aggregated weighted priority value; maximize rate of fault detection)
sut: Banking application (Java, JDK 1.6): 5 test cases, 5 faults (toy example); LOC not reported
leveraged feature: customer-allotted priority, implementation complexity, requirement changes (volatility), fault impact, completeness, traceability of requirements linked to test cases
notes: Text file starts mid-paper (title/abstract/intro page missing; begins at related work), so classification based on method + results sections. Weights per factor not given; no replication package.
title: A New Effective Test Case Prioritization for Regression Testing based on Prioritization Algorithm

algorithm_family: heuristic (greedy/rule-based: Non Redundant HGS and Enhanced HGS, extensions of Harrold-Gupta-Soffa with GRE redundancy removal)
objectives: single-objective (minimize test suite size subject to full branch-coverage requirements)
sut: FIRST_RUN PL/SQL procedure of a Payroll Management System (Oracle 10g, 33 relations; industrial-style/in-house): 512 LOC, average suite size 142 tests, 92 branch requirements, 5 branch-coverage-adequate test suites with varying redundancy
leveraged feature: requirements (branch coverage) matrix of test cases, associated testing sets and their cardinality
notes: Compared with HGS and GRE. Pseudocode and environment given; no code/data link. Fault detection loss not evaluated; single small subject.
title: Test Suite Reduction Using HGS Based Heuristic Approach

algorithm_family: hybrid (machine learning defect predictors: RF, LRM, GBRT + greedy total/additional/max prioritization)
objectives: single-objective (maximize APFD / defect detection rate)
sut: Gzip (SIR): 5,680 LOC, 279 tests, 37 injected defects; Grep (SIR): 10,068 LOC, 669 tests, 47 defects; Flex (SIR): 10,459 LOC, 447 tests, 32 defects; Sed (SIR): 14,427 LOC, 261 tests, 27 defects
leveraged feature: statement coverage of tests, statement-level defect-proneness probability from code metrics (keywords, operators, operands, lines)
notes: Coverage-based prioritization weighted by predicted statement defect probability (hybrid Coverage + Probability). WEKA default settings, cross-project training; no code/data link, so 0.5.
title: A novel test case prioritization method based on problems of numerical software code statement defect prediction

algorithm_family: program analysis (deterministic static/dynamic analysis: graph-database queries joining version-control revisions with code coverage)
objectives: single-objective (select tests covering the modified files/methods)
sut: OMICRON electronics diagnostic software suite (industrial, C++/C#/VB/C): >2.5 MLOC, 392 manual test cases with coverage data for two modules, 12 modifications analysed
leveraged feature: code changes from versioning systems (revisions, modified files/methods), per-test code coverage (files, methods, lines)
evaluation metric: number of selected test cases (file-level vs method-level)
notes: Tool prototype Sherlock (graph DB, NCover, SVN/TFS); experience report, no replication package (only an MSDN URL). Fit: change-to-coverage mapping resembles Modification-based; coverage-based redundancy hints.
title: Towards Tool-Support for Test Case Selection in Manual Regression Testing
